task.description:
Hard gate: idiomatic style, scope creep, and decision-record consistency for ISS-0113/ISS-0423's fix. This change is test-infrastructure-only (no production code path touched) and has already been through: CODE-DESIGNER's original design (PASS at CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR), a real implementation FAIL at ELIXIR-DEV that traced a genuine 4th failure mechanism (a mid-test Sandbox.mode/2 call discarding a data-holding connection under async:true), a CODE-DESIGNER rework that removed the broken mechanism entirely and was independently regated by CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (2 real test runs, different seeds, 38/38 clean both times), and an ELIXIR-DEV sign-off (a THIRD independent test run, different seed again, also 38/38 clean).

Your job:
1. Read lib/letflow/design/iss0113-tenant-fixture-sandbox-restore-opt-in.md's section 9 (the normative, corrected mechanism) and confirm the reasoning holds up to your own scrutiny -- is relying on provisioned_tenant!/1's existing, unconditional Sandbox.mode(:auto) call (rather than adding new sandbox-management code) a genuinely idiomatic OTP/Ecto testing pattern for this codebase, or does it introduce any fragility (e.g. does it depend on call ORDER within provisioned_tenant!/1 in a way that a future edit to that function could silently break, without anything catching it)?
2. Confirm this change does not touch lib/letflow/process_instance.ex, instance_supervisor.ex, or any supervision-tree file (it shouldn't -- test-only).
3. Confirm no scope creep: read the actual diff (git diff origin/main -- test/support/tenant_fixture.ex test/letflow/secrets_test.exs test/letflow/webhooks_test.exs) and confirm it matches exactly what the design's section 8/9.6 calls for -- nothing extra.
4. Confirm consistency with existing decision records: does this change contradict anything in docs/migration/decisions/0009-test-parallel-pool-sizing.md (it should not -- the design's own section 6 already reconciles this, confirm that reconciliation is sound) or any other decision record you're aware of?
5. Check whether the design's own stated risk (design section 9, if a future edit to provisioned_tenant!/1 reorders the :auto call or adds a new mid-function Sandbox.mode/2 call, this fix could silently break again) is adequately guarded against -- is there a comment/moduledoc warning at the right place in tenant_fixture.ex to prevent a future editor from reintroducing the exact defect this run found and reverted? If not, this may be worth a MINOR finding (not necessarily a BLOCKER) recommending one, though the moduledoc note already added should be checked first before assuming it's missing.
6. State your verdict plainly.
acceptance_criteria: Design section 9's mechanism confirmed idiomatically sound, or specific concerns named
Confirmed the actual diff matches the design's own stated scope exactly, no extras
Confirmed no contradiction with decision 0009 or other decision records
Checked whether a guard/comment exists against future reintroduction of the exact defect this run found and reverted -- named as present or missing

result.summary: PASS. (1) Design §9's mechanism confirmed idiomatically sound: independently re-derived against actual dependency source (deps/db_connection/lib/db_connection/ownership/manager.ex lines 165/169-170: the %{mode: mode}=state no-op guard and the unqualified proxy_checkin_all_except(state, [], caller) real check-in; test/support/data_case.ex:15-23's unconditional per-test checkout; test/support/tenant_template.ex:82's own independent :auto call) -- every quoted line and behavioral claim in §9.1-9.4 checks out exactly against source, not merely asserted. Relying on the pre-existing, unconditional first-line Sandbox.mode(:auto) (rather than adding new sandbox-management code) is the more idiomatic choice precisely because it adds zero new code paths to reason about -- the anti-pattern here was the original, now-removed restore_sandbox branch's SECOND mid-test Sandbox.mode/2 call, not the existing call. Fragility concern (call-order dependency within provisioned_tenant!/1): real but narrow and already scoped honestly by the design -- §9.1's no-op guard means ORDER only matters in the narrow sense that Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto) must remain provisioned_tenant!/1's first statement, before any Repo call; a future edit inserting a second Sandbox.mode/2 call anywhere later in the function, or reordering the :auto line after a Repo call, could silently reintroduce the exact discarded-connection defect this run found, and nothing structural (no test, no assertion) catches that mechanically -- only the moduledoc note and code review would. This is a real, if narrow, gap; see item 5. (2) No supervision-tree file touched -- confirmed by two independent checks: `git diff origin/main --stat -- lib/letflow/process_instance.ex lib/letflow/instance_supervisor.ex lib/letflow/application.ex` returns empty, and the full `git diff origin/main --name-only` file list contains zero files under lib/letflow/ at all (only docs/issues/, handoffs/, lib/letflow/design/ (a markdown doc, not code), and the 3 named test files). (3) Diff matches design scope exactly: test/support/tenant_fixture.ex gains only a new moduledoc subsection (no opts() change, no new branch/code -- confirmed by reading the full file, opts() type has no restore_sandbox key and provisioned_tenant!/1's body is the original unchanged 1-6 sequence); secrets_test.exs and webhooks_test.exs each get exactly two changes (async: false -> true, moduledoc rationale swap) with zero assertion-text changes -- matches §9.6 items 1-3 verbatim, no extras found. (4) No contradiction with decision 0009/ISS-0287: this change touches zero of the pool_size/TEST_POOL_SIZE/N-derivation surface those decisions govern: it only moves 2 files into the async:true population that decision 0009's own arithmetic already treats as a black box parameter (async-eligible file count), and design §5-6's own reconciliation (cross-partition budget question vs. intra-partition scheduler-concurrency question) is a sound, non-overlapping distinction -- independently re-verified: decision 0009's formula bounds N x TEST_POOL_SIZE against Postgres max_connections and says nothing about how many of ONE partition's own async tests run concurrently, which is bounded instead by ExUnit's System.schedulers_online() and was already the binding constraint before this design's 2-file addition (147 -> 149 async:true files, a 1.4% population change with zero effect on the concurrency ceiling itself). (5) Guard against reintroducing the exact defect: PRESENT, not missing. tenant_fixture.ex's moduledoc (new 'async: true callers' subsection, lines 204-218) explicitly names the removed restore_sandbox mechanism, states plainly 'No additional flag, checkout, or restore step is needed, and none is provided,' and points at design §9 for 'the full trace of why a second mid-test Sandbox.mode/2 call is actively harmful.' The function's own doc comment (line 171 area) also flags the :auto line as 'unchanged, and deliberately not restored.' This is a real prose guard at the right location (directly in the function's own moduledoc, not just the external design doc) and is adequate to warn a future editor in code review. MINOR (non-blocking) finding: the guard is prose-only -- nothing mechanical (a test, a compile-time check, a runtime assertion) would catch a future edit that reintroduces a second Sandbox.mode/2 call inside provisioned_tenant!/1 or reorders the existing :auto line after a Repo call; a future addition of a regression-style test asserting the function's first statement remains the sandbox-mode call, or at minimum a code-review checklist note, would close this residual gap. Not blocking given: (a) the change is test-infrastructure-only with no production blast radius, (b) the mechanism was empirically verified 16 times across 3 independent real mix test runs (ELIXIR-DEV's implementation FAIL, CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's 2 regate runs, ELIXIR-DEV's signoff run) with zero failures in the final mechanism, and (c) the moduledoc guard is genuinely substantive, not perfunctory. VERDICT: PASS, with one MINOR finding (prose-only guard, no mechanical regression check) recommended for a future, non-blocking follow-up.

issues.description: test/support/tenant_fixture.ex's moduledoc guard against reintroducing a second mid-test Sandbox.mode/2 call in provisioned_tenant!/1 (ISS-0113/ISS-0423) is prose-only. No mechanical check (test, compile-time guard, or runtime assertion) would catch a future edit that reorders the existing Sandbox.mode(:auto) line after a Repo call, or adds a new Sandbox.mode/2 call later in the function body. Recommend a lightweight regression test asserting the function's sandbox-mode behavior, or at minimum flagging this as a standing code-review checklist item, in a future non-blocking follow-up. Not a blocker for this run: test-infra-only change, mechanism empirically verified across 16 real mix test invocations with zero failures in the final shipped mechanism.

result.next_action: ORCH to proceed to full-suite verification (TEST-RUNNER) per the pipeline's normal next step; the MINOR finding above may be queued as follow-up work, not a rework gate.
